title: Preventing Injection and Input Errors knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should happen at an external trust boundary?
options: Trust client-submitted roles and ownership fields.
Return secrets in logs to simplify debugging.
Treat incoming data as unknown, validate its structure and policy, then create a trusted domain value.
Cast it to the desired interface and skip validation.
questions.answer_key: Treat incoming data as unknown, validate its structure and policy, then create a trusted domain value.
questions.explanation: Compile-time types do not validate external values or enforce authorization by themselves.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Preventing Injection and Input Errors”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with validating untrusted inputs and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with validating untrusted inputs and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Validating untrusted inputs”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Preventing Injection and Input Errors”?
options: Check safe database and command interfaces, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume avoiding unsafe html and string handling is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check safe database and command interfaces, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Safe database and command interfaces”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
